pr.title: List a pull request's unresolved review threads in its panel drawer
pr.head: 1ad98dc65ec469849f30f8fb3cb8bc3018dd79bf

summary: Projector's panel sits above the Claude Code prompt and lists the pull requests that the session's review and fix loops track. Each row ends with notes, and the last note counts the pull request's unresolved review threads, such as 2*. Pressing a pull request's number opens its drawer, a few lines of facts, actions, and links under the row.

Before this change, the count was the only trace of those threads, and GitHub can make them hard to find. It folds an outdated thread away, and on a long timeline it hides older threads behind Load more. A user saw 1* on three pull requests and could not find the thread on GitHub.

This change lists each unresolved thread at the end of the drawer, oldest first, as a link to the thread's first comment. Each line names the file and line, who opened the thread, the first line of its first comment cut to 60 characters, and outdated when a later push changed the lines the thread is on. The background poll still asks only whether each thread is resolved, as before. A second query fetches the details for the one pull request whose drawer is open.

The first review found that putting the details in the poll made each poll cost about one GitHub GraphQL point per tracked pull request, which could exhaust the account's hourly quota. The second commit moved them into the drawer's own query, and the re-review measured the poll back at 1 point for 51 pull requests and the drawer's query at 1 point.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Panel: the list of tracked pull requests and inbox items above the prompt.
  • Drawer: the lines a row opens when you press its number.
  • Poll: the panel's one gh api graphql call for every tracked pull request, at least every 30 seconds while the panel is shown.
  • Drawer query: the second call, for the open drawer's pull request alone, that fetches each unresolved thread's first comment.
  • Point: GitHub's unit of GraphQL cost. An account gets 5,000 points an hour, shared by everything that uses its token.
  • Outdated thread: a thread whose lines a later push changed. GitHub reports no current line for it, only originalLine.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• First review, at e9a5982: one P1. The poll's GraphQL cost grew with the number of tracked pull requests, from 1 point to 52 for 51 pull requests.
  • Fixed in 1ad98dc: the poll asks only isResolved again, and the drawer fetches its own threads. Re-measured at 1 point for the poll and 1 for the drawer's query.
  • Clean at 1ad98dc, with the validation gate passing.
  • Left out on purpose: marking a thread answered when its last comment is the operator's, because the review loop posts as the same account.

groups.title: The poll counts threads, and a second query reads them
groups.kicker: What the panel asks GitHub for, and when.
intro: The poll still asks only whether each thread is resolved, and a pull request in the snapshot keeps openThreads, a count. A new Thread type holds what the drawer lists: the file path, the line (or the line it was on, once outdated), whether it is outdated, who opened it, the first line of its first comment, and that comment's URL.

buildThreadsQuery asks for those fields for one pull request, and parseThreads keeps the unresolved threads. GitHub's GraphQL API cannot filter threads by whether they are resolved, so the query reads the first comment of every thread. The comment's bodyText is GitHub's plain-text rendering, which drops Projector's HTML comment markers and bold markup, so a Projector finding's first line reads P2 · ….

The split exists because of GitHub's rate limit. A connection nested under reviewThreads(first: 100), such as each thread's comments, costs about one point per pull request. Every reload sends the poll, at least every 30 seconds, so the poll stays free of it.

checks.text: The poll sends one query for every tracked pull request, including closed ones, so its cost scales with the tracked file's length. It costs about one point for each 50 pull requests.

files.note: Adds the Thread type and the panelThreads session state that holds the open drawer's threads. PullRequest keeps openThreads.
Splits the query builder so the poll and the drawer's query share it, adds THREAD_FIELDS, buildThreadsQuery and parseThreads, and factors the response reading into dataOf and nodeAt.

checks.text: Measured with rateLimit { cost } on this head's query text: a live poll of 10 pull requests costs 1 point, a dry run of 51 costs 1, and the drawer's query for one pull request costs 1. At the previous head the poll cost 10 and 52.

A live query on this repository confirmed that GitHub returns threads oldest first, that an outdated thread has line: null with an originalLine, and that bodyText starts a Projector finding with its priority.

files.note: Checks that the poll's query asks for no comments, and that parseThreads reads a resolved thread, an outdated one, a comment on a whole file, and a failure.

groups.title: The drawer lists the threads as links
groups.kicker: When the drawer reads its threads, and how it draws them.
intro: loadThreads fetches the open drawer's threads when the drawer opens and after each poll while it stays open. It skips the call when the poll counted no unresolved thread, drops an answer if another drawer opened meanwhile, and keeps the previous list when GitHub cannot answer. The threads live in panelThreads, keyed by the drawer, so the snapshot keeps its earlier shape.

threadLabel builds each line: the place, the author, the excerpt cut to 60 characters with an ellipsis, and outdated when it applies, joined by · . Each line is a Link element whose children are that text, so nothing in a path or a comment is read as Markdown. Each thread gets a line of its own, because a terminal without hyperlinks draws a link's URL after its text.

files.note: Adds fetchThreads and loadThreads, calls them from load and from toggle, and draws the open drawer's threads as links.

checks.text: Every way a drawer opens goes through toggle, including the digit hotkeys, which press the same buttons. Closing a drawer or opening an inbox item's drawer sends no query.
The drawer has no height cap, so a pull request with many open threads adds one line per thread above the prompt. The review asked the author whether that fits a short terminal.

files.note: Checks that the poll never asks for comments, that a drawer asks only for its own pull request and only when it has an open thread, that it asks again on each poll while open, and that it keeps its list when GitHub is unreachable.
